extracted.intended_audience: government officials, press regulators, journalists and media organisations (particularly in Jammu & Kashmir)
extracted.subtask_description: A fact-finding report setting out standards, findings and concrete recommendations to protect journalism, restore media access and regulate government–media interactions in Jammu & Kashmir. Targets administrative practice, press bodies, and media-policy reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic status vs unlawful activity
rubrics_metrics.description: If journalists ferry arms, provide support and harbour militants, or take part in any other unlawful activity, then they cease to be journalists and become militants or public persons supporting militants, and cannot claim any of the privileges that go with newspersons relaying and communicating news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited (e.g., Adil Farooq caught ferrying hand grenades). The report separates criminal acts (treat as militants) from legitimate journalistic work; those committing crimes should be prosecuted as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection for critical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: News and views may not be always palatable to those who are in power. Penalizing or charging journalists for news content merely because it is not in consonance with what the security forces or government administration believe is unjustified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tendency to label critical reporting as ‘anti-national’ or to arrest journalists for sedition must stop; governments should not penalize the messenger for reporting or quoting sources even if unpalatable to officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure uninterrupted communication access for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Restricting internet services for journalists (e.g., internet darkness after abrogation of Article 370, limited 2G workstations) is an extreme measure which muzzled the normal functioning of the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating token facilities (4 workstations/2G) for hundreds of journalists is inadequate. Cutting mobile towers and suspending internet prevents real-time coverage and fuels rumours; such restrictions should be reversed or proportionate and temporary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore press accreditation and privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: Press accreditation in the J&K region is an important passport for safe passage and preventing harassment and detention when traveling in conflict zones; not issuing accreditation reduces access and is a form of harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accreditation stopped since March 2020; accreditation and norms for press recognition and travel should be restored forthwith to allow movement, access to restricted areas and government offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow access to conflict scenes consistent with safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Severe restrictions on reporting live encounters (wide cordons, keeping media at bay, cutting mobile towers) prevent newsgathering; journalists should be allowed to perform their duties as professionals as long as they do not hinder normal security operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security may restrict proximity for safety, but must brief media and not permanently deny access. Balance safety concerns with journalists’ need for timely reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit intrusive profiling and irrelevant questionnaires
rubrics_metrics.description: Summoning journalists to fill questionnaires seeking answers on matters unrelated to journalism (e.g., political allegiance, property details, relations in Pakistan) is improper and suggestive of implying links with ‘anti-national’ forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profiling programmes aimed at journalists should be stopped; questions unrelated to professional accreditation are an abuse and intimidatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure freedom to travel and return personal equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Exit Control Lists (ECL) that blacklist journalists from traveling abroad, refusal/complications in passport renewal, confiscation of personal communication equipment, and requiring bonds before issuing internet connections are discriminatory practices that impede journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ECL use and passport renewals must not be arbitrarily applied to journalists; confiscated equipment should be returned; bonds or preconditions for internet access to journalists should be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect independence of journalist representative bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative bodies of journalists (e.g., Kashmir Press Club) should be allowed to function; arbitrary de-registration, suspension of elections, takeover of premises and interference by administration or police undermine press freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restore registration of bodies like the KPC; government officials should not interfere in internal elections; orders keeping registration ‘in abeyance’ must be justified and transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process for government accommodation allotments
rubrics_metrics.description: Removal of journalists and news organisations from government-allotted accommodation cannot be arbitrary and without due process of law; criticism of government is not a legitimate ground for repossession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where no proper grounds have been served, accommodation should be restored; a clear written policy should regulate allotment and return so decisions are not dependent on officials’ whims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral and fair government advertising allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Government advertisement should not be used to reward politically favourable media or punish critical outlets; advertisements should be released without taking political affiliation or editorial policies into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The J&K government must review slanted practices. The report recommends forming an advisory committee including DIPR officials, media owners and journalist representatives to ensure fair allocation; police should not be part of such a forum unless matters involve breach of peace or criminality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial appeals mechanism in media policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellate committees provided in the New Media Policy should not be staffed entirely by government officials; aggrieved publications must have access to independent evaluation of appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise appellate provisions to include media organisation representatives or eminent civil society members to ensure independent review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent verification of readership/viewership
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocation of government advertising often depends on circulation/viewership numbers; these should be certified by independent bodies (e.g., RNI for newspapers, BARC for TV) rather than internal or partisan measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An independent body should certify readership/viewership to prevent manipulation of advertising allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stop misuse of draconian laws against journalists; distinguish crime from reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Intimidation, arrests and detention under draconian laws (e.g., UAPA) have been used against journalists; while those indulging in criminal acts should be prosecuted, writing against government policies must not be treated as criminal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report records many arrests (49 since 2016; 8 under UAPA). Authorities must stop treating critical reporting as ‘anti-national’ and misusing severe laws to thwart journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cease police takeover of departmental public relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations work of various government departments being taken over by the Police is inappropriate and against democratic norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR functions should be handled by respective departments; if Police require spokespeople, they should be appointed only for police matters and not represent other departments by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase and appoint departmental spokespersons for access
rubrics_metrics.description: Insufficient number of official spokespersons makes it hard for journalists to obtain the government’s version of events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appoint additional spokespersons for both Kashmir and Jammu divisions so journalists have access to official explanations; this will reduce rumours and improve information flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore normal privileges of newsgathering
rubrics_metrics.description: Restricted internet facilities, denial of accreditation, suspension of mobile connectivity during conflicts and denial of access to coverage and travel are methods developed to choke free and fair newsgathering; these policies must be reversed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must be allowed to work professionally; restrictions should only be used when strictly necessary for security and in proportionate ways; restoring communications reduces misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set up Media Advisory Committee for dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish platforms for discussion (a 3-way Media Advisory Committee among the security establishment, government officers and journalist representatives) to encourage dialogue and address grievances and ease mutual suspicion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press Council can have a role on such an advisory body; the Editors Forum supported the idea. Such committees should be inclusive and help resolve conflicts on access and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and oversight for digital news networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Large numbers of digital channels and social-media-based news platforms have no entry barriers or oversight; there should be a survey and registration process to ensure legal due diligence and observance of journalistic ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend neutral, autonomous bodies (e.g., Indian Readership Survey, BARC) conduct surveys and registration so digital networks are subject to basic norms of journalism and law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure support for Urdu-language publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Government departments have suspended purchase/subscriptions of Urdu publications and Urdu outlets are reportedly handicapped in advertising allotments due to administrative shortcomings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restore subscriptions and advertising support for Urdu publications; fill DIPR staffing shortages so Urdu publications receive fair treatment and balance with other languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide insurance and health cover for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists working in an active conflict zone risk injury or death; previous promises for medical and accident insurance cover for accredited journalists have not been implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The current government should implement the scheme (draft notification and seed money were earlier prepared in 2018) and ensure insurance and health cover is provided at the earliest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in administrative decisions affecting press bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Orders keeping registration or re-registration of press bodies ‘in abeyance’ or reversing earlier verification must disclose reasons, underlying reports and timelines for final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: KPC received non-involvement certificate then re-registration; later an SSP, CID report led to registration being kept on hold without reasons. Authorities should disclose grounds and expected timelines for decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect editorial independence from external pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and journalists should not be pressurized by authorities or others to change wording or adopt labels (e.g., being pressured to replace ‘militants’ with ‘terrorists’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial choices are a professional responsibility; undue pressure on language or framing is an interference with journalistic independence and should cease.
